evidence_completeness_definition: Fraction of six required run-provenance fields present.

findings.summary: Any authenticated user can read any invoice because ownership, tenant, and permission checks are absent.
findings.evidence: canReadInvoice returns true whenever user.authenticated and invoice are truthy.

findings.summary: The document listing returns every supplied document without restricting results to the user's tenant.
findings.evidence: listDocuments(user, documents) directly returns documents and never uses user.

findings.summary: A charge failure after reservation leaves the reservation in place, with no rollback or recovery mechanism.
findings.evidence: processOrder awaits gateway.reserve before gateway.charge but has no error handling or compensation.

findings.summary: Older status events can overwrite newer order state because event sequence ordering is not validated.
findings.evidence: applyStatus unconditionally assigns event.status and event.sequence to the order.

findings.summary: Redelivery or retry of a payment message can charge the customer multiple times.
findings.evidence: processPayment invokes provider.charge without an idempotency key or duplicate-message check.

findings.summary: Emitting individual user IDs as request attributes creates an unbounded telemetry dimension.
findings.evidence: requestAttributes assigns request.userId to the "user.id" attribute.

findings.summary: The project pins Log4j Core 2.14.1, a version affected by the Log4Shell remote-code-execution vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228).
findings.evidence: pom.xml declares org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core version 2.14.1.

findings.summary: Nested retry loops invoke the operation up to nine times, amplifying load and side effects during failures.
findings.evidence: Three outer iterations each contain three inner attempts, with no backoff or retry filtering.

findings.summary: The migration immediately drops a column, risking data loss and failures in application instances that still reference it.
findings.evidence: migration.sql contains only ALTER TABLE accounts DROP COLUMN legacy_status.

findings.summary: Any authenticated user can read any invoice, regardless of ownership or permissions.
findings.evidence: canReadInvoice returns true solely when user.authenticated and invoice are truthy; it never compares tenant, owner, role, or access grants.

findings.summary: The document listing function returns documents without tenant filtering.
findings.evidence: listDocuments ignores user entirely and returns the complete documents collection.

findings.summary: A successful reservation is left active when the subsequent charge fails.
findings.evidence: processOrder calls gateway.reserve before gateway.charge but has no compensation, cancellation, or recovery handling for charge failure.

findings.summary: Older status events can overwrite newer order state.
findings.evidence: applyStatus unconditionally assigns event.status and event.sequence without rejecting an event whose sequence is not newer than order.sequence.

findings.summary: Repeated delivery of the same payment message can produce duplicate charges.
findings.evidence: processPayment directly invokes provider.charge without an idempotency key, deduplication record, or processed-message check.

findings.summary: Per-user identifiers create an unbounded telemetry attribute dimension.
findings.evidence: requestAttributes emits request.userId as the "user.id" attribute for every request.

findings.summary: The project pins a Log4j version affected by the Log4Shell remote-code-execution vulnerability.
findings.evidence: pom.xml declares org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core:2.14.1, which is affected by CVE-2021-44228.

findings.summary: Nested retry loops invoke a failing operation up to nine times per logical call.
findings.evidence: The three-iteration outer loop contains a three-iteration inner loop, and every inner iteration calls operation().

findings.summary: The migration immediately drops a column, breaking callers that still read or write it and preventing simple rollback.
findings.evidence: migration.sql contains only ALTER TABLE accounts DROP COLUMN legacy_status, with no staged deprecation, compatibility period, or data-preserving recovery step.

findings.summary: Any authenticated user can read any invoice, regardless of ownership, tenant, or permission.
findings.evidence: canReadInvoice returns true whenever user.authenticated and invoice are truthy; it performs no object-level authorization check.

findings.summary: Document listing exposes records across tenant boundaries.
findings.evidence: listDocuments returns the complete documents argument without filtering it by the requesting user's tenant or access rights.

findings.summary: A charge failure after a successful reservation leaves the reservation uncompensated.
findings.evidence: processOrder awaits gateway.reserve, then calls gateway.charge without rollback, cancellation, or reconciliation when charging fails.

findings.summary: Stale or duplicate events can overwrite newer order state.
findings.evidence: applyStatus assigns event.status and event.sequence unconditionally, without verifying that the incoming sequence exceeds order.sequence.

findings.summary: Duplicate message delivery can charge the customer multiple times.
findings.evidence: processPayment directly invokes provider.charge on every call and supplies no message identifier, idempotency key, or deduplication check.

findings.summary: Using individual user IDs as telemetry attributes creates unbounded cardinality.
findings.evidence: requestAttributes emits request.userId as the "user.id" attribute, potentially creating one attribute value per user.

findings.summary: The project pins a Log4j version affected by the actively exploited Log4Shell vulnerability.
findings.evidence: pom.xml declares org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core:2.14.1, a version affected by CVE-2021-44228 and listed through that vulnerability in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

findings.summary: One logical call can invoke the failing dependency nine times immediately.
findings.evidence: Nested loops each iterate three times around operation(), producing 3 × 3 attempts with no backoff, jitter, deadline, or retryability classification.

findings.summary: The migration immediately and irreversibly removes account data and breaks code that still reads or writes the column.
findings.evidence: The sole statement is ALTER TABLE accounts DROP COLUMN legacy_status. Rivet's migration inspection classified the DROP as a critical destructive operation; no compatibility window or recovery mechanism is present.
